absent: Zonelist construction policy and fallback ordering beyond verification printing.
Full struct layouts, field offsets, sizes and padding for zone, node, page and per-CPU cache.
Default values of watermark scale factor, high fractions, boot batch and high, list counts, shuffle order and retry, and zone type enumeration.
Lock ordering across zone lock, batch mutex, node lock and reclaim paths.
Reclaim thread main loop, watermark enforcement, slab and compaction interaction.
Error handling and return contracts for allocation failure, offline nodes and sparse holes beyond what is shown.
Timing, concurrency and memory ordering guarantees beyond observed single writes and locks.

findings.text: Boot diagnostic verifies zonelist ordering when verbosity reaches verify level. For each online node it walks every combination of zonelist kind and zone index, skips zones without pages, emits a debug line identifying node and zone, then walks the fallback list for that starting index printing node and name of each entry. An alternate header provides an empty definition used when the diagnostic is compiled out.

Per-CPU page cache initialization clears both the cache and statistics structures, initializes its spinlock and each free-list head, and installs conservative boot values for batch and high watermarks. Zone setup allocates per-CPU storage for caches and statistics where supported, initializes each CPU copy, then recomputes tuned high and batch values. Updates to live caches propagate new batch and high bounds to every possible CPU using ordered single writes.

Batch size balances allocation latency against zone lock contention. With address translation enabled it starts from the smaller of a tiny fraction of managed pages and a 256 KiB equivalent page count, returns one if tiny, otherwise rounds to one less than a power of two to reduce cache color aliasing when tasks interleave batches. Without address translation it always returns one to avoid deferring frees and fragmenting large contiguous runs needed for high-order requests.

Per-CPU high threshold derives either from the zone low watermark or from managed pages divided by a configured fraction. The total is divided among CPUs local to the zone node plus an adjustment for a CPU coming online, falling back to all online CPUs when the node has none, and is clamped to at least four times batch. When a manual fraction is configured minimum and maximum high collapse to the same value disabling auto-tuning; otherwise minimum uses the watermark basis and maximum uses a small built-in fraction. Cached zone values suppress redundant propagation.

Watermark recomputation serializes the global update with a private static spinlock and then refreshes every zone cache tuning. Cache tuning itself serializes through a dedicated batch and high mutex. Per-zone watermark fields are mutated with the zone lock held in interrupt-safe mode.

Minimum reserve starts from a global kilobyte reserve converted to pages and distributed across zones in proportion to managed pages relative to total low memory excluding high memory and movable kinds. High memory and movable zones instead receive a small capped reserve bounded below and above. Low, high and promotion levels add a distance that is the larger of one quarter of the proportional share and a scaled fraction of managed pages, with boost cleared and total reserves recomputed afterward.

Startup watermark initialization in order refreshes the global minimum reserve, rebuilds per-zone levels, refreshes statistics thresholds, rebuilds low memory reserves, optionally rebuilds unmapped and slab minima on NUMA, and notifies huge-page balancing. The global reserve derives from free buffer pages converted to kilobytes, scaled and square-rooted, then clamped within fixed bounds unless a user-provided value takes precedence, in which case a rate-limited warning is emitted.
Per-node unmapped and slab minima are zeroed for every online node then accumulated from each zone managed page count multiplied by the corresponding system control ratio as a percentage.

Per-CPU statistics thresholds scale logarithmically with online CPU count and zone size in 128 MiB units, capped at a fixed maximum. Refresh zeroes node thresholds, installs per-zone values on every online CPU, promotes each node value to the largest of its zones, and arms a drift mark at high watermark plus total possible drift when aggregate per-CPU drift could hide a breach of minimum while free pages appear above low.

Isolation release expands the requested page frame interval outward to pageblock boundaries and steps block by block, locating the first online page in each block and skipping blocks without an isolated page. Successful release decrements the zone isolated-block count. A large free block spanning the target is removed, its isolation flag toggled, and split; otherwise free pages migrate between isolate and recorded type lists before the flag toggles. A state mismatch triggers a one-time warning and failure without change.

Clearing isolate from a pageblock first handles a free buddy at or above block order by attempting to extract it so later merging can proceed, warning if extraction unexpectedly fails. If no such extraction occurred the block is released through the generic unisolate and move path with a warning on zone-boundary failure; otherwise the isolate flag is cleared directly and the extracted page returned to the tail of the appropriate free list. The zone lock is held throughout and the operation is a no-op if the page is no longer isolated.

Isolation release holds the zone lock in interrupt-safe mode via scoped guard, and returning an isolated page asserts that lock is already held. Free-list shuffling holds the same lock interrupt-safe while swapping entries, periodically dropping it and yielding to avoid long hold times.

Shuffling randomizes free-list order at a fixed block order to reduce predictability. It aligns the zone interval, validates each candidate block head, then makes bounded random attempts to find a distinct valid partner within the zone span. Partners with mismatched migration types are skipped with debug output. Valid partners exchange list membership. A static key gates the whole pass, and an alternate build provides an empty operation.

Per-node reclaim thread startup takes a node identifier, locks node thread state, and creates a node-bound thread named for that node only if none exists. Creation failure logs the node and error, treats failure before full system operation as fatal, and leaves no thread recorded; success wakes the new thread. The node lock is released in all paths.

Observed state includes per-CPU cache with lock, list array, batch and high bounds; zone with per-CPU cache and statistics pointers, cached high and batch tunables, watermark array with boost, isolated-block count and drift mark; node with zonelist array, zone array, reclaim thread pointer and unmapped and slab minima; and per-CPU statistics with a flush threshold. Watermark indices distinguish minimum, low, high and promotion levels.

Fixed numeric bounds observed are maximum statistics threshold one hundred twenty five, global reserve clamp between one hundred twenty eight and two hundred sixty two thousand one hundred forty four, movable and high memory minimum clamp between a cluster constant and one hundred twenty eight, high clamped to at least four times batch, and batch derivation from managed pages shifted by twelve versus a 256 KiB equivalent.

Stale cache tunables after watermark changes cause premature reclaim or excess retention, so watermark updates always refresh caches. Splitting large buddies during isolate transitions avoids stranding mergeable pages. Shuffling only swaps pages of equal order, zone, buddy state and migration type to avoid corrupting segregated free lists. Random partner search is bounded to avoid unbounded scanning of sparse zones.

Global interfaces provided to other memory management components include zone cache setup, watermark setup and initialization, minimum reserve calculation, free buffer accounting, pageblock unisolate helpers, isolated page return, isolation range release, zone shuffling control, statistics threshold refresh and threshold computation, and per-node reclaim thread startup.
